stories.title: UK announces £600 million package to strengthen AI security and biosecurity
stories.summary: The UK announced a roughly £600 million package focused on AI-related health and security risks. Plans include a government-backed AI Biosecurity Lab, up to £200 million in AI model credits from OpenAI and Anthropic, additional support for the AI Security Institute, and an AI-enabled centre to detect cyber threats. More implementation and funding details are expected with the Budget.
stories.why: The package links frontier-AI development to practical safeguards against biological and cyber threats. Its impact will depend on how quickly the labs become operational and how independent, transparent their evaluations are.

stories.title: Critical PHP vulnerabilities trigger urgent patching warnings
stories.summary: Two critical PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, can under certain conditions lead to unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP released fixed versions on October 21, and security agencies are urging operators to inventory internet-facing systems and patch promptly. Researchers have reported exploitation attempts, but reports do not establish successful compromise in every case.
stories.why: PHP remains widely deployed in web servers and applications, so vulnerable installations can expose services to serious compromise. Prioritize supported fixed versions, especially on public-facing systems.

stories.title: Iranian officials say Tehran has plans to target Gulf undersea cables if war resumes
stories.summary: Two Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel renew attacks. This is a reported conditional threat, not a report that cables have been cut. Analysts say the immediate impact would likely be regional because less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, but multiple cuts could disrupt Gulf connectivity and complicate repairs.
stories.why: Subsea cables support cloud services, financial transactions and regional internet access. The threat highlights how conflict can endanger digital infrastructure as well as energy and shipping routes.

stories.title: GameMaker will make its GMRT runtime free for commercial releases from January 2027
stories.summary: GameMaker says developers will be able to build and commercially distribute GMRT games on desktop, mobile, web and GX Games without a Professional licence starting January 1, 2027. Source-code access will be available across tiers. Console exports will still require an Enterprise licence and approved-developer status.
stories.why: The change lowers the upfront cost for indie developers choosing a 2D-focused engine and increases competition among game-development tools. Console publishing remains a separate paid path.

stories.title: Vietnam's coal-fired electricity reaches a record as export manufacturing expands
stories.summary: Reuters analysis citing Ember data says Vietnam generated 132.9 terawatt-hours of coal-fired electricity in the first nine months of 2026, up 15% year over year. Stronger manufacturing demand and lower hydropower output contributed to the increase; coal supplied about 52% of the power mix and power-sector emissions also rose.
stories.why: Vietnam's export growth is increasing electricity demand while much of its supply remains coal-dependent. This creates energy-security and emissions challenges and may bring greater scrutiny from overseas buyers of Vietnamese-made goods.
